title: Consolidate telemetry shims, async histogram sink, and adaptive sampling
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our runtime and control-plane services currently depend on several ad-hoc telemetry wrappers and different OpenTelemetry SDK versions. This causes duplicated serialization logic, high tail allocations in the Prometheus exporter path, and inconsistent sampling behavior across services (leading to noisy traces and occasional memory pressure during high-load experiments).

Goal: Reduce telemetry-related CPU/memory overhead and unify tracing/metrics integration so that:
- Span/metric encoding is handled by a single lightweight shim package used by all services.
- We replace the current synchronous histogram exporter with an async histogram sink (batching + bounded worker pool) to eliminate per-request blocking on exporter IO.
- Introduce an adaptive sampling policy (runtime-configurable) that reduces traced-span volume during SLO pressure while preserving representative traces for regression detection.

Success criteria (measurable):
1) 25-40% reduction in telemetry-related p99 CPU on the runtime during synthetic load tests.
2) Span drop rate < 1% after rollout; end-to-end request latency regression < 2ms median caused by telemetry path.
3) No increase in OOM incidents attributable to tracer allocations in the 30-day canary window.
4) All services compiled against OTEL SDK >= 1.20.0 and telemetry-shim v1.0.0 released.

Scope:
- Audit and extract common serialization + tag-normalization into telemetry-shim package (Go).
- Implement async histogram sink that batches histogram updates and writes to the metrics backend (supports prometheus remote_write and direct TSDB ingestion).
- Update tracing hooks to use OTEL semantic conventions and the new shim API; migrate top 10 services by request volume.
- Add adaptive sampling controller (config via feature flag + console toggle) and export sampling diagnostics as low-cardinality metrics.

Out of scope: full replacement of existing logging libraries, agent-side instrumentation for third-party integrations, or end-to-end change to application-level metrics naming conventions (will be follow-up).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Moving to a batch/async sink increases time-to-observe for histograms by up to 5-10s; mitigated by exposing a fast-path metric for recent errors and allowing TTL on critical counters.
- Adaptive sampling removes some detailed traces under load; to mitigate, sampling controller keeps prioritized traces for errors and tail latency.
- Upgrading OTEL SDK will require audit of any custom instrumentation shims; we will gate upgrades behind compile-time flags and CI smoke tests.

Plan (high level):
1) Feb week 1: Audit (list of services + call sites) and propose shim API.
2) Feb week 2-3: Implement telemetry-shim (serializers, tag normalizer) + unit tests.
3) Feb week 4: Implement async histogram sink + integration tests (local TSDB and remote_write emulation).
4) Mar week 1: Migrate 3 low-risk services and run performance benchmarks.
5) Mar week 2: Gradual rollout to top services with canary window and automatic rollback if span drop > 1% or OOM regressions.
6) Post-rollout: cleanup old exporters and document migration guide.

Rollout & monitoring:
- Canary 1: api-runtime-a (5% traffic) for 72 hours, monitor span throughput, CPU, memory, and request latency.
- Canary 2: control-plane services (config-rollouts) for 48 hours.
- Key dashboards: telemetry-pipeline-health (span rate, exporter latency), runtime-cpu-by-component, memory-alloc-by-service, span-drop-rate, sampling-controller-decisions.

Implementation notes:
- Target Go 1.21 for shim to leverage recent allocation improvements.
- Use a bounded worker pool for async sink; default pool=8 with tunable per-service override.
- Keep a compatibility layer in shim to support older SDKs while services migrate (deprecation planned for 3 months after release).

Deliverables:
- telemetry-shim v1.0.0 (Go module) + CHANGELOG.
- async-histogram-sink implementation + tests and Helm values for tuning.
- sampling-controller with console toggle and diagnostics metrics.
- migration playbook for engineers and runbook for on-call.
